historical_record.description: The United States Housing Authority approved the Holly Park project here, San Francisco's first public housing, on vacant land the Board of Education had bought for a school it never built; an old fire station on the site was to be removed. Arthur Brown Jr. was its architect and L. Glenn Hall its landscape architect.

Barrett and Hilp won the general construction contract for Holly Courts at $373,787; ground was broken on July 7, 1939, the first project of the federal housing program west of the Rockies to start building.
Holly Courts, 118 apartments in two-story concrete buildings, was completed and accepted by the Housing Authority, and was fully occupied soon after.
